note: Presets are saved parameter sets for the same animation; they do not count as additional animations. All content is fictional and illustrative (jurisdiction unspecified). The total and every value are hypothetical placeholders labelled as such; segment lengths follow only the supplied values. Scene A uses the values supplied under allocation A, scene B those under allocation B; by default they differ in one boundary only. No share rule or legal doctrine is stated and nothing is attributed, ranked or decided; both stages have equal weight. Long-labels-stress: coordinator decision (standing stress-cap rule, docs/AUTHORING.md item 20, from LAW-0687/0689–0692; per-scene subject floor >= 0.20 of the frame height as in accepted LAW-0707/0711). True driver: the 9:16 and 1:1 boxes — each of the two stages (rail, shelf, trays, floor) must stand >= 0.20 of the frame height while every text stays >= 16 px. Fallbacks tried: stages side by side and stacked, the panel below (chips packed two to a row) or beside, compact rail zones, staggered value chips, bare-number value chips with the unit named in the head chips, a guide band between heads and rails. Measured, rendered at 1080p (2026-10-05; pre-cap copy production/scratch/causation-10/LAW-0719.stress-precap.json): full counts (four events, two totals described, two accounts put forward, one labelled connector, two shared facts) → 1:1 no composition fits (fallback), 9:16 per-stage height 0.177; one total, one account, no connector note, one shared fact → 9:16 0.199. The stress keeps the maximum four events and caps the rest at the baseline's: one total described, no account put forward, no connector note, one shared fact (baseline 1 / 0 / 0 / 1); every text field keeps its near-maximum length. After the cap: 9:16 0.202 (18 px), 1:1 0.265 (17 px), 16:9 0.376 (17 px).
